program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s criterion already distinguishes a frog clearly inside the bowl from one merely on the lid, but its question/binding are too broad to expose that distinction reliably. The edited image shows one frog inside the bowl, while other frogs are on the raised lid and floor; the repeated traces all claim completion with high confidence, yet the aggregate reference is partial. Refine the typed criterion and evidence request to assess the requested placement specifically against the source image, distinguishing bowl interior from lid/rim/floor and recording each location before assigning the outcome. Do not treat extra frogs as either fulfillment or failure by themselves. The traces are valid, queried, and dependency-free, so this is not a transport/schema failure; investigate the semantic mismatch between their confident ‘inside’ judgments and the aggregate label rather than forcing the reference label or assuming the edit is absent. Repeated identical judgments are not independent confirmation.
